questions.q: What does a generative model do?
options: It learns a data distribution and draws new samples from it
It stores images and retrieves the closest one
questions.answer: It learns a data distribution and draws new samples from it
questions.why: Fit p_θ(x), then sample from it.

questions.q: The copier in the lab has a good distance score. Why is it still not a good model?
options: None of its samples are new, and it gives unseen data no density
Its samples are all in the gap between modes
questions.answer: None of its samples are new, and it gives unseen data no density
questions.why: Its "new samples" column is 0.000. Sample quality alone cannot detect this.

questions.q: Why is log-likelihood measured on held-out data?
options: Because a model that memorised scores well on its own training data
Because training data has no likelihood
questions.answer: Because a model that memorised scores well on its own training data
questions.why: Unseen data shows whether the model learned the distribution.

questions.q: What did the one-Gaussian model get wrong?
options: It put a third of its samples in a gap where the data almost never goes
questions.answer: It put a third of its samples in a gap where the data almost never goes
questions.why: 0.326 against 0.016. Too few parameters cause blur between separate modes.

questions.q: Is it correct to say diffusion models can never reproduce a training image?
options: No, some training images have been extracted, mostly heavily duplicated ones
No, they store a copy of every image
questions.answer: No, some training images have been extracted, mostly heavily duplicated ones
questions.why: Carlini et al. 2023 extracted some images. Models are neither databases nor proven free of copying.
